vlog_arc.theme: August launch week — putting a real offer in front of people for the first time after a month of near-zero tracked sales. Own the gap, fix the engine in public.

beats.mon: Leo opens the week at 5am, formula on the desk, and says it straight: last month I sold almost nothing I could actually track. Not because the coffee failed, because I never put a real offer in front of anyone. This week I fix that in public.
beats.tue: Leo explains the one change that matters this month: a real starting offer, the 15-day pack plus the free recipe book, and why he stopped hiding the price. Product in the cup, not pitched.
beats.wed: Leo reacts to the first UGC video a creator made for the brand. He talks about hearing his own product described back to him by a stranger, and what 'one scoop into the coffee you already make' really means.
beats.thu: Leo reads a real customer review out loud, pauses, and connects it to why he paid to get the formula independently certified: he wanted proof he could stand behind, not louder claims.
beats.fri: Leo closes the laptop at 4pm to get the kids, then shares the week's real numbers with no spin (orders, ebook opt-ins) and names the first-100-ship-free push as his line in the sand.
beats.sat: A quiet Saturday training session, no music, then a cup at the desk. Leo reflects that a launch is not one big moment, it is showing up with an offer every single day.
beats.sun: Leo looks at next week's plan, names the one thing he is most uncertain about (will paid traffic convert), and commits to publishing the number either way.

ig.title: You know the 2pm crash. I lived it for years.
ig.angle: Founder Reel 1, but the CLIENT is the hero. Strong hook on the client's own 2pm crash (third coffee, still foggy, the afternoon gone). The launch is only the reason to act now (the real offer finally goes live this week), never the point. Product as the receipt. Cover phrase all caps. Engagement prompt asks about THEIR afternoon. CTA to betterday.
